Distribution and trusted brands reduce the cost of introducing adjacent products, while procurement and
manufacturing scale support availability and cost control. These advantages are most valuable when they produce
repeat purchases and better returns on incremental capital. They do not eliminate the need to spend on
advertising, channel incentives and new facilities.
Aashirvaad, Sunfeast, Bingo!, YiPPee!, Classmate and personal-care brands give ITC exposure to consumption
beyond tobacco. The competitor set differs by category: HUL in personal and home care; Britannia and Parle in
biscuits; Nestle and regional brands in packaged foods; Godfrey Phillips and VST in legal cigarettes. This is an
analytical competitor map, not a market-share ranking.
ITC Hotels is separately listed and accounted for as an associate in ITC group reporting. Buying ITC today does not
confer the historic demerger distribution on a new buyer. Our earnings-multiple valuation includes subsidiary and
investment income within standalone earnings; it does not add a separate hotels stake value on top.

Gross sales can rise while the underlying franchise earns less
ITC states that, following expiry of GST Compensation Cess, GST and central excise on cigarettes increased from 1
February 2026. GST and compensation cess are excluded from gross product revenue, whereas excise is included.
The tax change therefore distorts period comparisons of reported gross revenue and inventory values. [D]
The simple bridge differs from the company presentation metric. The presentation reports an operating net-revenue measure, while
financial-statement excise and other operating revenue have different scope/timing. This report does not force the two definitions to
reconcile. Forecasts use a separately defined revenue-from-operations less excise measure.
Full tax pass-through can protect unit profit while damaging volume; partial pass-through protects price points but
sacrifices margin. Consumers can downtrade within the portfolio or migrate to illicit supply. A staggered approach
buys time for the franchise, but near-term accounting earnings absorb the cost. The sustainable outcome depends
on both legal volume retention and net revenue per stick.
Management describes staggered pricing and portfolio interventions. The company does not disclose a clean,
independently auditable cigarette volume series in the reviewed statements. Broker volume estimates are
therefore excluded from the base dataset. We do not infer volumes from gross revenue. [U]
FY27E cigarette EBIT of Rs 14,800 crore is about 30% below FY26. FY28E EBIT of Rs 16,900 crore still remains about
20% below FY26. This assumes some pricing repair without requiring a full reversal of the tax burden. A strong
brand can survive a tax reset while its shareholders earn a lower return.

Scale needs to translate into higher profits and capital returns
*Q1 FY27 10.0% EBITDA margin is the company presentation measure excluding Sresta; it is not directly comparable to the unadjusted annual
segment EBITDA margins. Annual segment figures include intra-group revenue; they are not additive to group external sales. [B, F]
Management reports broad growth in dairy, snacks, noodles and frozen foods, supported by premiumisation and
newer channels. Its July FAQ says digitally enabled sales plus modern trade account for 34% of FMCG sales
excluding education and stationery, versus 17% in FY20; UNNATI covers over 8 lakh outlets. These are
company-reported channel measures, not independent market-share evidence. [G, U]
The segment uses meaningful capital. FY26 EBIT divided by average segment assets less segment liabilities is about
17.6%, compared with an exceptionally high ratio in cigarettes. This is a pre-tax segment-capital proxy, not formal
ROIC: it omits corporate assets, treasury and tax, and acquisitions can distort it. The takeaway is directional:
revenue diversification is currently less profitable than the original franchise.
A 100-basis-point EBIT margin gain on FY26 FMCG revenue would add about Rs 242 crore of EBIT and Rs 0.14 of
EPS after 25% tax. A 10% decline in FY26 cigarette EBIT would remove about Rs 2,105 crore of EBIT and Rs 1.26 of
EPS. FMCG margin expansion matters, but cannot quickly neutralise a large tobacco shock.

Paper expansion and technology optionality add execution risk
FY26 standalone segment revenue was Rs 8,766 crore and EBIT Rs 797 crore, a 9.1% margin; FY25 EBIT was Rs 911
crore. Q1 FY27 showed improvement, but the segment remains sensitive to wood, energy and imported paper
pricing. ITC completed its Century Pulp and Paper acquisition on 1 August 2026. The earlier agreement specified
consideration of up to Rs 3,500 crore on a cash-free, debt-free basis. [A, K]
Our FY27 revenue assumption includes roughly seven months of the acquired operation and a larger capital base.
This is acquisition-led scale as well as an operating recovery. The relevant test is incremental free cash flow after
maintenance capex and working capital, rather than consolidated tonnes or revenue alone.
FY26 segment EBIT was Rs 1,496 crore on gross segment revenue of Rs 20,296 crore. Annual accounts show about
Rs 8,000 crore of intra-group revenue. Commodity and export revenue can be large relative to margins, so
external sales, earnings and working capital deserve more weight than the segment revenue headline. [A]
A poor crop can raise input costs while limiting availability; a strong crop can support volumes while pressuring
commodity realisations. Export restrictions, freight disruptions and foreign exchange add further variability. We
forecast gradual EBIT growth and do not capitalise a temporary commodity windfall.
ITC Infotech and Happiest Minds: proposed, not completed
The 31 August filing proposes purchase of 22.106% of Happiest Minds for about Rs 1,330 crore in two tranches,
followed by amalgamation into ITC Infotech. The scheme proposes listing ITC Infotech; the disclosed swap is 25
ITCI shares for every 81 HMTL shares held by eligible shareholders other than ITCI. Approvals and closing
Potential benefits are scale, cross-selling and a transparent listed valuation. Risks include integration, AI-driven
pricing pressure, the cash contribution via ITCI rights funding and dilution of ITC economic ownership in the
combined subsidiary. The base forecast includes existing subsidiary dividends within net unallocated income, with
no assumed listing windfall, merger gain or guaranteed dividend accretion.
Century consideration up to Rs 3,500 crore, the Rs 645 crore Sproutlife balance purchase and proposed Rs 1,330
crore technology stake purchase sum to about Rs 5,475 crore. This is a cash-demand envelope, not a claim that all
was paid in one period. It excludes other acquisitions, fees, taxes and transaction adjustments.

Cash stewardship matters as much as reported growth
ITC has no identified promoter/promoter group in the reviewed company filings. Sanjiv Puri is Chairman and
Managing Director; Supratim Dutta is Director and CFO in the FY26 accounts. Institutional ownership and an
experienced board are useful governance features, but they do not substitute for scrutiny of acquisition
economics, related-party transactions and capital returns. [A, L]
Secondary-source category totals from Screener, rounded; foreign classification may include strategic overseas corporate holdings. Do not
read 33.22% as pure tradable FPI ownership or add separately quoted BAT holdings to it. This is not a beneficial-ownership audit. [O]
Governance questions for the next twelve months
Track whether acquisition consideration and rights subscriptions remain inside disclosed terms; whether
consolidated returns improve after goodwill and intangible amortisation; and whether subsidiary cash can be
remitted without impairing operations. A separately listed ITC Infotech could improve transparency, while also
creating a new minority-interest and capital-allocation framework.
ESG: operational progress and tobacco exposure coexist
ITC reports renewable-energy use, water stewardship and sustainable sourcing programmes. Those programmes
can lower operating risk and support supply resilience. They do not remove the health harm and regulatory
exposure of tobacco, or the investment exclusions applied by some institutions. We retain a lower valuation than
many consumer peers because these constraints affect both future cash flows and the investor base.
The FY26 group accounts disclose Rs 1,235.64 crore of claims not acknowledged as debt, including the specified
share of associates; estimated capital contracts not provided for were Rs 1,634.40 crore. These are disclosed
exposures rather than forecasts of actual cash loss. The ultimate timing and outcome are uncertain. [A, printed
Our model does not assume a large litigation loss. A significant adverse ruling, impairment, acquisition overrun or
sustained dividend funding from asset sales would require a reassessment of both earnings and valuation.

Keep facts, definitions and estimates distinct
Issuer financial statements and exchange filings anchor reported earnings, balance sheets, cash flow and
transactions. Presentations and FAQs provide management operating measures. Investing.com supplies the dated
NSE price, and Screener supplies raw peer ratios and ownership categories. All online sources were accessed on 31
October 2026. Company disclosures are not independent verification of market share or management claims.
Financial years end 31 March. Q1 FY27 is April-June 2026. September-quarter figures are not published ITC results
in this report. Annual FY26 accounts were audited; Q1 statements received limited review. Standalone figures
drive the forecast and P/E valuation; consolidated figures are shown separately to capture subsidiaries and the
distinction between total group and attributable profits.
